neighbours.label: function words inside an expository definition of a technical concept ('a technique that attempts to ...', 'focuses on ...', 'meaning that ...')
fire: Garbage collection is a form of memory management that tries to reclaim objects no longer in use.
A compiler is a program that translates source code into machine instructions.
Dropout is a regularization method that aims to prevent a network from overfitting.
Caching is a strategy that stores recent results so they can be reused quickly.
Public key cryptography is a scheme that relies on a pair of mathematically linked keys.
Gradient descent is an algorithm that seeks to minimize a function by following its slope.
A mutex is a lock that ensures only one thread can enter a section at a time.
Version control is a system that records changes to files over time.
quiet: Yesterday the garbage collector froze our game for two seconds during the demo.
My compiler crashed again this morning, so I went for a coffee.
We turned dropout off last night and the training run looked worse.
The caching server in our office was rebooted twice on Friday.
I forgot my key password again and had to call the help desk.
Our gradient descent run finished late, so we left the lab after midnight.
Tom spent all afternoon chasing a mutex bug in the old code.
She lost a week of work before her team started using version control.

notes: Top examples are all definitional technical prose (hypertext, list reversal, HTTP/1.1, fractals, transfer learning). Probe: definition 0.81 and 0.22, casual sentence 0.00. Near misses keep the technical topic but are narrative, not definitions. The + pole is causal connectives (because of, due to, thanks to).
